en: The nose, the group of odors, water, salt, the throat, and the series [of phonemes], as well as the state of dryness.
The saltiness of the ocean reached to the tip of his nose; the necklace upon his throat was like the rainy season; the dust upon his head, indicative of passion, was like a consecration with jewels;
and the assembly of his kinsmen was like a gathering of gems.

May the Sun, who possesses the luster of moving gold, whose rays are like streaks of light, and who is the source of the syllable *trāṃ*—may he, the bearer of the jewel, long bestow upon us the state beyond the fourth (*triturya*). *rekhāvedanavedanācayacalaccāmīkarābhiḥ* (possessing the luster of moving gold from the mass of sensations perceived as lines);

*rekhā vedanavedanā ca* (and the sensation of pain is a mere line); *yat* (who); *calaccāmīkarābhaḥ* (having the appearance of moving gold); *ciraṃ* (for a long time); *sūrye* (in the Sun); *trāṃkṛtijaḥ* (born from the syllable *trāṃ*); *dadātu* (may he grant); *maṇibhṛt* (the bearer of the jewel); *yātmatṛtrituryadharam* (that which transcends the three and the fourth).
May Maṇibhṛt, born from the syllable *trāṃ*, grant a boon to Sūrya as his third self.

The letter *Ha* is the bamboo-stalk for the waves of ideation (*saṃjñā*), the mercury-essence for the thunderbolt of aesthetic flavor (*rasa*), the sprinkling of the thunderbolt of passion (*rāga*), the springtime for the flowers born from the sour fruit of the aggregate of ideation,
the lotus-cluster on the banner-lotus of the lake of the tongue’s observation, and the faultless abode of the fourth state.
Red in color, born from the syllable Hīḥ, he possesses a splendor like that of Amitābha and, with a radiant luster, [attains] meditative absorption. || 5 ||

The body of the aggregate of formations (*saṃskāraskandha*) is the summer heat of the green horse (*hayagrīva*), the envy that performs the rite of the *kṛtyā*, the sword-banner, the family of the dyer, the raw meat, the girdle, and the midnight.
The form of contact (*sparśa*) is the labial class (*pa-varga*); it is the consecration of the wind, the jewel, the vajra, and the bell.
Born from the syllable Khaṃ in the sun, Amoghasiddhi, the green one who bestows fearlessness, removes all fear. (6)
Immediately [appearing], delightful with a vajra and bell shimmering with the essence of a luster as white as camphor;
a true commitment (*susamaya*) arising from regions of affliction (*sopakleśa*); having exhausted the dregs (*kaṣāya*);
and possessing the sixth consecration (*ṣaṣṭhābhiṣeka*) of meeting with most cooling splendors until dawn.
May the discourse on the glorious dharmadhātu bestow glory, and may Vajrasattva, born from the syllable HŪṂ, do the same. || 7 ||

May Locanā— born from the seed-syllable *laṃ*, marked by the wheel (*cakra*), possessing the luster of nectar, having the earth as her nature, resembling the moon, purified of the delusion of delusion, and consisting of loving-kindness (*maitrī*)— be for your welfare. (8)
The water element is presided over by Karuṇā; she is black and born from the syllable MĀṂ.
As Māmakī, she quickly accomplishes [the rite] through the vajra of hatred, O Moon.
The lotus-dweller situated in the moon is red, having the nature of the fire element;
she is born of joy, and Pāṇḍarā is marked by pure passion.
Dark-complexioned, purified by the breeze, free from envy, and bearing a blue lotus;
with hands like lotuses, she is the supreme Tārā, born from the syllable *Tāṃ*, the destroyer of Māra.
May the yellow Vajriṇī, enriched with the qualities of the hare-marked moon, born from the nectar of the solar orb,
and accompanied by her jewel, bestow upon you pure freedom from slanderous intent.

And by way of identity, Locanā and the others are sealed by the five [Buddhas] beginning with Buddha with their own respective seals; furthermore, these Buddhas and the rest are sealed by Dveṣa (Aversion), and Dveṣa is sealed by Vajradhara; through that distinction from Śāśvata (Eternity), he too is Vajradhṛk.
Therefore, know now that this entire universe is purified by the union [of the two], through the Guru. 13.
Having composed this work in five aspects, may the world, through the abundant merit earned by the virtuous Bhaṭṭa Ratnākara, become the Holder of the Vajra (Vajradhṛk). 14.
Thus ends the *Pañcākāra* composed by Bhaṭṭa Ratnākara.
